metadata.description: The ownership and isolation border. Every record carries a tenant_uuid resolving to one of these, and it is the referent ownership, cost attribution, audit scope, drift accountability, and policy scope all agree on. A member belongs to exactly one at a time — a structural lock, not a convention — and tenants may nest, the child keeping its resources and its isolation while the parent holds governance overlay and rollup.

provider_ref.description: The auth-capability provider that evaluates this expression (cardinality-1 URF).

expression.description: OPAQUE provider-scoped subject expression — an LDAP DN, an OIDC claim, a K8s subject. Never parsed or evaluated by UDLM.

subject_bindings.description: The RBAC bridge: external subject-expressions whose holders this grouping is FOR. Opaque by design — parsing or evaluating one would re-import the permission engine the model excludes.

membership_criterion.description: The RULE that derives the member set — a stored URF filter (identifier-scheme 9; declared fields only, URF-005), never the set itself. Idioms: tenancy "estate?tenant_uuid=={self}" (exclusivity is structural — the field is scalar); ownership "estate?owned_by=={self}"; labels "estate?labels.concern==payments"; explicit set "estate?uuid=in=(a,b)" — the marked exception, prefer any derivable form; exclusion "estate?tenant_uuid==abc;member_of!=access/groupings/hold".

obligations.description: REQUIRED here, where the base leaves it optional. A tenant IS an isolation border, so how strongly it isolates is not something to leave unsaid: `none` is a deliberate declaration, not an omission. The mechanism that delivers a level (row-level security, separate stores, separate hardware) is the implementation's choice and is not modelled here.

parent_group_uuid.description: The parent tenant this one nests inside (§4). A child tenant keeps complete isolation — its resources belong to it and never to the parent (GRP-INV-004) — while the parent holds governance overlay, cost rollup, and audit aggregation. Absent means a root tenant. Destroying a parent requires explicit resolution of every child first; there is no silent cascade (GRP-INV-003).

context.purpose: The ownership and isolation border. Every record in the model carries a tenant_uuid pointing at one of these, and it is the referent that ownership, cost attribution, audit scope, drift accountability, and policy scope all resolve against.
context.plain_description: A tenant. A thing belongs to exactly one at a time, and that is a structural lock rather than a convention — crossing the border is a deliberate, recorded act, not a default. Tenants may nest: a child keeps its own resources and its own isolation, while the parent gets governance overlay, cost rollup, and audit aggregation across its children.
use_when: Something must have exactly one owner, and moving it between owners must be visible
You need a boundary that cost, audit, drift, and policy all agree on
You are modelling a business unit, a customer, or a team that owns infrastructure
not_for: Grouping without isolation — a cost centre, a project, a label. That is a plain Grouping, where a member may belong to many and enforcement is advisory
Deciding who may act — external RBAC owns that (ADR-008); this decides what belongs to whom
Permitting one tenant to use another's resources — that is Grouping.Authorization
works_with: Grouping.Authorization — the recorded exception that lets a relationship cross this border
Every estate record — tenant_uuid resolves here (TEN-001/003, [D3])
The governance matrix — isolation obligations are enforced over the derived member set
